title: First Tor is R-linear in its second argument
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and M an R-module. Let F be the functor N ↦ Tor'_1(M,N) on the category of R-modules, with Tor' derived in its first argument [def-weil-pbc-tor-modules]. This functor is additive [lem-weil-pbc-tor-one-second-additive] and for any R-modules X,Y, R-linear map f : X → Y and r ∈ R, F(r • f)=r • F(f); equivalently F is R-linear.

proof.text: Fix the projective resolution P of M once for all coefficient modules. By the definition of Tor' and Mathlib ProjectiveResolution.leftDerived_app_eq, its map on a coefficient homomorphism f is the degree-one homology map of P tensor f, conjugated by the fixed comparison isomorphisms for the source and target. These isomorphisms depend on the objects, not on f.

proof.text: Use the proved additivity instance to give the Functor.Linear predicate its required Functor.Additive structure. Tensoring on the right takes r • f to r times its natural transformation: evaluate at a module Z and use the tensor-product scalar identity. Passing to mapHomologicalComplex and evaluating on P preserves this scalar multiplication degreewise. The local proved helper torHomology_map_smul identifies degree-one homology of the scaled chain map with r times homology of the original: the shortComplexFunctor preserves scalars componentwise and ShortComplex.homologyMap_smul applies. Finally Linear.smul_comp and Linear.comp_smul move r through the fixed comparison morphisms. Thus F(r • f)=r • F(f), which completes Functor.Linear R.
